evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The current manager_restarted check only verifies nonzero, differing manager PIDs and nonempty, differing invocation IDs. It does not verify that both manager snapshots came from the same guest boot. A guest reboot during the manager phase changes both PID and invocation ID, so it can falsely satisfy manager_restarted; a later reboot can then satisfy the separate boot_id_changed check. Requiring nonempty and equal boot IDs on the manager before/after snapshots is the smallest compatible correctness fix.
